column2: description
The ultimate uniform load per purlin line (or equivalent applied pressure) reached when the test assembly failed, the primary strength result of each test.
Description of how the assembly failed (local buckling, lateral movement, brace or fastener failure), used to interpret the measured strength.
Bending moment in the purlin corresponding to the measured failure load, the strength result expressed as a moment.
Air-pressure differential in the vacuum chamber at the instant of failure, the raw measurement from which line loads are computed.
Rotation of the purlin cross-section computed from paired potentiometer readings, showing torsional response.
Applied load at which buckling of the roof deck was first observed, an intermediate event prior to failure.
Yes/No record of whether the predicted limit state was the one actually observed in the test.
Horizontal (lateral) movement of the purlin cross-section derived from the paired potentiometer readings, with its two components and total.
Uniform load back-calculated from the measured support reactions at each increment, cross-checking the manometer pressure.
Maximum tensile and compressive stresses in the purlins computed from the strain gage readings during the test.
Displacements of the purlins and deck measured by potentiometers and by optical survey at each load increment.
Strains recorded by gages on the purlin cross-sections and on the bracing straps at each load increment.
column21: sensor_1 … sensor_66 (gage numbers vary by test)

column2: Load-cell reaction measured under a purlin at exterior and interior supports at each load increment, used to check load distribution and continuity.
Yield stress of the purlin steel measured on tensile coupons, the key material input to computed capacities.
Percent elongation of the tensile coupon at fracture, a measure of the steel's ductility.
Ultimate tensile strength of the purlin steel from coupon tests, reported alongside yield stress to characterise the material.
Measured thickness of the tensile coupon machined from the purlin web, reported separately from the section thickness.
Measured width of the reduced section of the tensile coupon, needed to compute coupon stresses.
Depth of the purlin cross-section, the dominant geometric parameter governing bending stiffness and strength.
Shape of the cold-formed purlin cross-section (C or Z), which changes the bending and torsional behaviour.
Base-metal thickness of the purlin sheet steel, measured on the section or taken from the designation, controlling local buckling and capacity.
Effective section modulus of the purlin computed by AISI effective-width rules, used to obtain the theoretical bending strength.
Width of the purlin flange, measured or nominal, which controls local buckling of the compression flange.
column23: TOP Flange Width (inches), BOTTOM Flange Width (inches)

column1: Purlin lap length at interior support
column2: Overlap length of the lapped purlins at an interior support in continuous assemblies, affecting negative-moment strength.
Length or vertical dimension of the edge stiffening lip on the purlin flange, which stiffens the flange against local buckling.
Gross moment of inertia of the purlin cross-section about the bending axis, computed from the measured dimensions.
Angle between the edge stiffening lip and the flange it stiffens, a key geometric variable for stiffener effectiveness.
column23: TOP Lip Angle (degree), BOTTOM Lip Angle (degree)

column2: Inside bend radii at the web-to-flange and flange-to-lip corners of the cold-formed section.
Gross (unreduced) section moduli of the purlin referred to the top and bottom extreme fibres.
Unbraced length taken as the distance from the end of the lap to the theoretical inflection point, used in lateral-buckling checks.
Measured failure load or moment divided by the corresponding computed capacity, the headline measure of prediction accuracy.
Ratio of required to nominal strength at the failure load, including the AISI shear-plus-bending interaction check.
Average experimental base-test reduction factors for compared parameter sets and the percent difference between them, used to judge whether a parameter matters.
Standing seam roof strength reduction factor from the AISI Base Test Method, applied to the purlin capacity (1.00 for through-fastened).
Ratio of interior to exterior support reaction, showing how much continuity the three-span assembly developed.
Uniform line load per purlin line predicted to cause failure by a code or base-test calculation, compared with the measured value.
Nominal or allowable flexural capacity of the purlin computed from the measured section and yield stress, the benchmark for the test moment.
Positive- and negative-region moments computed from a stiffness analysis of the continuous assembly, used in the prediction of failure load.
Nominal flexural strength assigned to the positive and negative moment regions of a continuous purlin under a given bracing assumption.
Nominal shear strength of the purlin web per AISI, and the shear demand at the failure load, used in the shear-plus-bending check.
Moment gradient coefficient Cb computed for the negative moment region in the lateral-buckling calculation.
Governing predicted limit state (positive moment, negative moment or combined shear and bending) for each assembly.
Allowable stresses for compression flange, tension flange and web used in the AISI capacity calculation.
Moments of inertia used in the strength and deflection calculations, together with the computed deflection per unit load.
Lateral bracing and anti-roll restraint provided to the purlins, a main variable affecting system strength.
Whether the simulated load acts downward (gravity) or upward (uplift), which changes which flange is in compression.
Number of parallel purlin lines loaded in the test assembly, which sets how load is shared.
Number of continuous spans in the tested assembly, distinguishing simple-span base tests from multi-span systems.
Type of roof sheeting attached to the purlins (through-fastened or standing seam, with gage and fastener details), which determines how much restraint the deck gives.
Span length between supports of the test assembly, the geometric condition that sets the moment for a given load.
Self weight of the deck and purlin per foot of purlin line, added to (or excluded from) the applied load when reporting failure load.
Centre-to-centre spacing of purlin lines (with deck overhang), which fixes the tributary width used to convert chamber pressure to line load.
column26: purlin spacing (note), 3.75 ft tributary width (note) [ft-in check]

column2: Whether the purlin top flanges face the same direction or are opposed, affecting system torsional behaviour.
Type of standing seam clip connecting the panel to the purlin (fixed or sliding, low or tall), a key restraint variable.
Whether blanket insulation was placed between the purlin flange and the panel, which reduces restraint.
Narrative notes on the test configuration or support detail that do not fit a numeric column.
Nominal sheet gage designation of the purlin material used in the test.
Number of individual base tests performed within a test series.
Safety factor of 1.67 (printed 1.65 in one heading) removed from the AISI allowable moment to form a reference capacity.
Label identifying each test or specimen, the key for joining all other data of that paper.
Which purlin line within the assembly (east/west, ridge/eave, interior/exterior) a measurement refers to.
Bookkeeping fields giving the table, page or date from which a reported value was taken.
Series or group label collecting tests that share configuration parameters.
Manufacturer of the roof decking used in each full-scale test.
Manufacturer designation of the Z-purlin section giving depth and nominal thickness.
